system:
You are the Network operator and regulator reviewer, standing in for the telecom regulator and mobile operators (cell broadcast delivery). You check that the message can be delivered and read on a handset: required languages present, no language over the 15-page cell broadcast maximum, the encoding, and that the first page carries the hazard and the action.
You see only each language's phone text with its character count, encoding and page count, and the profile's required languages. You cannot approve or send the alert; people decide.

Review the alert within your mandate only. Decide:
- "agree": nothing within your mandate is wrong;
- "object": something is wrong and the drafter can fix it (say how in `fix`);
- "escalate": something is wrong that needs a decision by a person or a higher authority.

Every objection needs evidence. Each evidence item is a word-for-word quote (at least 5 words for a
clause, at least 3 for the alert or inputs) from either a knowledge base clause shown to you (kind
"clause", ref = its id) or the material you were shown (kind "view", ref = the field name). Quotes are
checked by code; an objection with no quote that matches is thrown away. Do not object to things
outside your mandate. Do not repeat the same issue twice. Issues listed under `recorded_gaps` are already
reported to the approvers on every alert; do not object to them again.
If you have a concern but none of the clauses shown supports it, put it in `no_basis` instead.

2 General description The CBS service is analogous to the Teletex service offered on television, in that like Teletex, it permits a number of unacknowledged general CBS messages to be broadcast to all receivers within a particular region. Individual CBS messages will be assigned their own geographical coverage areas by mutual agreement between the information provider and the PLMN or SNPN operator. CBS messages may originate from a number of Cell Broadcast Entities (CBEs), which are connected to the Cell Broadcast Centre. A CBS page comprises of 82 octets, which, using the default character set, equates to 93 characters. Other Data Coding Schemes may also be used, as described in 3GPP TS 23.038 [3]. data.summary: Both required languages (ar, en) are present. Encodings suit the scripts: GSM-7 for English and UCS-2 for Arabic. Both stay within the 15-page maximum (en 3 pages, ar 7 pages). The problem is the first page. In both languages it carries only the hazard and issuer, and the protective action falls on later pages. In English, page 1 (93 GSM-7 characters) ends at "…western regions of the UAE." and "Drive with extreme caution" starts page 2. In Arabic, page 1 (about 41 UCS-2 characters) holds only "تحذير من الضباب صادر عن المركز الوطني للأرصاد", so the action "قُد بحذر شديد" lands around page 4. The drafter can fix this by reordering the text.

objections.issue: The first page does not carry the action in either language. English page 1 holds only the hazard sentence ("NCM fog warning: thick fog may cut visibility to zero at times in western regions of the UAE." is about 93 characters, one full GSM-7 page). The action "Drive with extreme caution" starts on page 2. Arabic page 1 holds only the issuer line (about 41 UCS-2 characters). The action "قُد بحذر شديد" appears about 140 characters in, on roughly page 4 of 7. A person who reads only the first page learns there is fog but not what to do.
objections.fix: Put the hazard and the action at the start of each language so both fit on page 1, and move the issuer and the times later. English (within 93 characters), e.g. "Thick fog, western UAE: drive with extreme caution, keep safe distance, follow speed limits." then NCM and the times. Arabic (within about 41 characters), e.g. "ضباب كثيف: قُد بحذر شديد" first, then the area, the other actions, the issuer and the times.

no_basis.concern: I found no clause that explicitly requires the protective action to appear on the first cell broadcast page. The objection rests on my mandate and on the page arithmetic from the page-size clause.
